evidence: Curt. 5.6: Prīmusque rēx dolābrā glaciem perfringēns iter sibi fēcit
terms.comment: The soldier’s and the labourer’s pick, for breaking hard ground, ice, and old walls.
The digger’s mattock of the fields; see “hoe”.

phrases.latin: Hīc solum dūrissimum est; dolābram affer.
phrases.english: The ground is very hard here; bring the pickaxe.

phrases.latin: Prīmusque rēx dolābrā glaciem perfringēns iter sibi fēcit
phrases.english: and the king himself was the first to break through the ice with a pickaxe and make a path

phrases.latin: Dolābrae cālōnibus dīviduntur ad vallum prōruendum fossāsque implendās.
phrases.english: Pickaxes are handed out to the camp servants for pulling down the rampart and filling in the ditches.

sources: Lewis & Short: dolabra · Lewis & Short: ligo
